identity.title: HvNCED12 positively regulates salt tolerance in barley by modulating abscisic acid biosynthesis and ion homeostasis.

content.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) biosynthesis is essential for plant salt tolerance, but the roles and upstream regulation of individual 9-cis-epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase (NCED) genes in barley remain unclear. To determine whether HvNCED12 contributes to barley salt tolerance and identify its upstream regulator, we generated CRISPR/Cas9 knockout and overexpression lines in the barley cultivar Golden Promise. Wild-type and transgenic plants were exposed to 150 mM NaCl for 14 d, with or without 100 muM ABA. ABA content, physiological traits, ion accumulation, and gene expression were measured, while promoter regulation was examined by yeast one-hybrid, electrophoretic mobility shift, and dual-luciferase assays. Salt induced HvNCED12 expression approximately sixfold at 24 h, and HvNCED12-GFP localized to chloroplasts. Under salinity, knockout lines showed reduced ABA and chlorophyll, 49.3% higher malondialdehyde content, disrupted Na(+)/K(+) homeostasis, and reduced biomass, whereas overexpression lines showed opposite responses. Exogenous ABA partially alleviated these defects and reduced malondialdehyde by 29.1% in knockout lines. HvNCED12 also affected ABA biosynthesis-, ion transport-, and stress-related gene expression. HvMYB10 bound the HvNCED12 promoter and activated transcription. These findings identify an HvMYB10-HvNCED12 module that promotes salt tolerance by regulating ABA biosynthesis and ion homeostasis.
